html:
The Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque in Bandar Seri Begawan was completed in 1958 and named after the sultan who built it, Omar Ali Saifuddien III. Its golden dome rises over a lagoon beside the water village.

It was paid for by the new oil wealth of Seria, and built in a mix of Mughal and Italian styles, with marble from Italy. A stone copy of a royal barge sits in the lagoon.

The mosque became the symbol of Brunei's idea of itself as a Malay Islamic monarchy, the theme later carried into its sharia laws. See also Islam.
